messages.body: Hello Lan, I'm Linh from the Hangyul Univ team. I'll be with you from the first document to arrival in Korea. Your checklist is ready in the app.
Thank you! I uploaded my passport and transcript. Do I need to translate the transcript myself?
No — we arrange the certified translation. Please only make sure the scan shows all four corners of every page.
Transcript scan is cropped on page 2 — asked for a new one. Bank certificate can wait until the visa stage.

Thank you for the feedback. I rewrote the second paragraph three times and I am still not sure it is right, so I am writing everything here. My family runs a small shop that imports Korean snacks, and since I was fourteen I have been translating the labels for customers — ingredients, allergy notes, storage instructions. Last year I made a one-page guide in Vietnamese for the forty best-selling products and the number of returned items went down. I want to say this clearly without sounding like I am exaggerating. Should I give the numbers (returns went from about 30 a month to 12), or is that too much detail for a personal statement? Also, the university asks for 800 words and I am at 1,140. Which part would you cut: the paragraph about my grandmother, or the one about the school exchange programme?
I left comments on your personal statement. Your story about translating snack labels is great — let's make the project result more concrete.

prompt.text: Introduce yourself and explain why you want to study Korean at our Language Institute. Describe your plan after completing the program. (800 words or fewer)

body.body:
I first heard Korean in my aunt's kitchen in Da Nang. She had worked in Daegu for six years and still counted change in Korean when she was tired. I was eleven, and I wanted to know what she was saying.

Since then I have studied Korean on my own for four years and reached TOPIK 3 last spring. I am very passionate about Korean culture and I believe that studying at Kyungpook National University will broaden my horizons. I chose the Korean Language Program because its level 4 curriculum includes the academic writing course I need before I apply to a degree in food science.

My family grows coffee, and every harvest we lose part of the crop to a drying process nobody has measured. In my last year of high school I logged the humidity of forty-two drying beds for three weeks and showed my father which beds to move. We lost less that year. It was a small project, but it taught me that careful measurement changes decisions.

After the language program I plan to apply to Kyungpook National University's School of Food Science and Biotechnology. In ten years I want to run a post-harvest laboratory in Dak Lak that serves small farms. I know Pusan National University also has a strong program, but Daegu is where my aunt's stories began, and it is where I want to begin mine.

body.prompt: Describe an experience that shaped your decision to study business. (student-pasted question)

findings.text: The text is much shorter than the limit allows (1,000 words).

body.body:
When customers at my family's shop in Hai Phong picked up a packet of Korean seaweed, they turned it over, looked at the label, and put it back. They could not read it. I was fourteen when I started writing Vietnamese labels by hand and taping them to the shelves.

Last year I made a one-page guide for the forty best-selling products. Returns went from about thirty a month to twelve. I learned that a business grows when a customer understands what she is buying, and that is why I want to study Business Administration at Pusan National University.

The BBA curriculum's Global Marketing track and the Busan port internship programme match what I want to learn: how products cross a border and still make sense on the other side. After graduation I plan to return to Hai Phong and build an import company that explains every product it sells.

body.title: Study plan — Pusan National University
body.body:
My study plan has three stages. In the first year I will complete the university's Korean for Academic Purposes courses alongside Principles of Economics and Business Statistics, so that by the second year I can take major courses taught in Korean.

In the second and third years I will concentrate on international trade and logistics. Busan is the largest port in Korea, and I intend to apply for the port-logistics field programme in my third year.

In the final year I will write a graduation project on cold-chain logistics for Vietnamese fruit exports. After graduation I plan to work for a logistics company in Busan for two to three years before returning to Vietnam.
